lines.text: Of such as have before endur'd the like.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Thus play I in one person many people,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: And none contented: sometimes am I king;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Then treasons make me wish myself a beggar,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: And so I am: then crushing penury

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Persuades me I was better when a king;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Then am I king'd again; and by and by

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Think that I am unking'd by Bolingbroke,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: And straight am nothing: but whate'er I be,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Nor I, nor any man that but man is

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: With nothing shall be pleas'd till he be eas'd

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: With being nothing.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Music do I hear?

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Ha, ha! keep time. How sour sweet music is

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: When time is broke and no proportion kept!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: So is it in the music of men's lives.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: And here have I the daintiness of ear

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: To check time broke in a disorder'd string;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: But, for the concord of my state and time,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Had not an ear to hear my true time broke.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: I wasted time, and now doth time waste me;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: For now hath time made me his numbering clock:

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: My thoughts are minutes; and with sighs they jar

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Their watches on unto mine eyes, the outward watch,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Whereto my finger, like a dial's point,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Is pointing still, in cleansing them from tears.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Now sir, the sound that tells what hour it is

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Are clamorous groans, which strike upon my heart,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Which is the bell: so sighs and tears and groans

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Show minutes, times, and hours; but my time

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Runs posting on in Bolingbroke's proud joy,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: While I stand fooling here, his Jack o' the clock.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: This music mads me; let it sound no more;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: For though it have holp madmen to their wits,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: In me it seems it will make wise men mad.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Yet blessing on his heart that gives it me!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: For 'tis a sign of love; and love to Richard

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Is a strange brooch in this all-hating world.

stage_directions: Enter a Groom of the stable.

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: Hail, royal Prince!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Thanks, noble peer;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: The cheapest of us is ten groats too dear.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: What art thou? and how comest thou hither, man,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Where no man never comes but that sad dog

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: That brings me food to make misfortune live?

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: I was a poor groom of thy stable, king,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: When thou wert king; who, travelling towards York,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: With much ado at length have gotten leave

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: To look upon my sometimes royal master's face.

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: O! how it yearn'd my heart when I beheld,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: In London streets, that coronation day,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: When Bolingbroke rode on roan Barbary,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: That horse that thou so often hast bestrid,

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: That horse that I so carefully have dress'd.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Rode he on Barbary? Tell me, gentle friend,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: How went he under him?

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: So proudly as if he disdain'd the ground.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: So proud that Bolingbroke was on his back!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: That jade hath eat bread from my royal hand;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: This hand hath made him proud with clapping him.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Would he not stumble? would he not fall down,--

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Since pride must have a fall,--and break the neck

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Of that proud man that did usurp his back?

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Forgiveness, horse! Why do I rail on thee,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Since thou, created to be aw'd by man,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Wast born to bear? I was not made a horse;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: And yet I bear a burden like an ass,

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Spur-gall'd and tir'd by jauncing Bolingbroke.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: Fellow, give place; here is no longer stay.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: If thou love me, 'tis time thou wert away.

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.text: My tongue dares not, that my heart shall say.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: My lord, will't please you to fall to?

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Taste of it first as thou art wont to do.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: My lord, I dare not: Sir Pierce of Exton,

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: Who lately came from the king, commands the contrary.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: The devil take Henry of Lancaster and thee!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Patience is stale, and I am weary of it.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: Help, help, help!

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: How now! What means death in this rude assault?

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Villain, thy own hand yields thy death's instrument.

stage_directions: Snatching a weapon and killing one.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Go thou and fill another room in hell.

stage_directions: He kills another, then EXTON strikes him down.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: That hand shall burn in never-quenching fire

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: That staggers thus my person. Exton, thy fierce hand

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Hath with the king's blood stain'd the king's own land.

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Mount, mount, my soul! thy seat is up on high;

lines.speaker: King Richard II
lines.text: Whilst my gross flesh sinks downward, here to die.

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: As full of valour as of royal blood:

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Both have I spilt;  O! would the deed were good;

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: For now the devil, that told me I did well,

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Says that this deed is chronicled in hell.

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: This dead king to the living king I'll bear.

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Take hence the rest, and give them burial here.

scenes.setting: Windsor. An Apartment in the Castle.

stage_directions: Flourish. Enter BOLINGBROKE and YORK, with Lords and Attendants.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Kind uncle York, the latest news we hear

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Is that the rebels have consum'd with fire

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Our town of Cicester in Gloucestershire;

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: But whether they be ta'en or slain we hear not.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Welcome, my lord. What is the news?

lines.speaker: Earl of Northumberland
lines.text: First, to thy sacred state wish I all happiness.

lines.speaker: Earl of Northumberland
lines.text: The next news is: I have to London sent

lines.speaker: Earl of Northumberland
lines.text: The heads of Salisbury, Spencer, Blunt, and Kent.

lines.speaker: Earl of Northumberland
lines.text: The manner of their taking may appear

lines.speaker: Earl of Northumberland
lines.text: At large discoursed in this paper here.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: We thank thee, gentle Percy, for thy pains;

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: And to thy worth will add right worthy gains.

lines.speaker: Lord Fitzwater
lines.text: My lord, I have from Oxford sent to London

lines.speaker: Lord Fitzwater
lines.text: The heads of Brocas and Sir Bennet Seely,

lines.speaker: Lord Fitzwater
lines.text: Two of the dangerous consorted traitors

lines.speaker: Lord Fitzwater
lines.text: That sought at Oxford thy dire overthrow.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Thy pains, Fitzwater, shall not be forgot;

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Right noble is thy merit, well I wot.

stage_directions: Enter HENRY PERCY, With the BISHOP OF CARLISLE.

lines.speaker: Henry Percy (Hotspur)
lines.text: The grand conspirator, Abbot of Westminster,

lines.speaker: Henry Percy (Hotspur)
lines.text: With clog of conscience and sour melancholy,

lines.speaker: Henry Percy (Hotspur)
lines.text: Hath yielded up his body to the grave;

lines.speaker: Henry Percy (Hotspur)
lines.text: But here is Carlisle living, to abide

lines.speaker: Henry Percy (Hotspur)
lines.text: Thy kingly doom, and sentence of his pride.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Carlisle, this is your doom:

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Choose out some secret place, some reverend room,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: More than thou hast, and with it joy thy life;

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: So as thou livest in peace, die free from strife;

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: For though mine enemy thou hast ever been,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: High sparks of honour in thee have I seen.

stage_directions: Enter EXTON, with attendants, hearing a coffin.

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Great king, within this coffin I present

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Thy buried fear: herein all breathless lies

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: The mightiest of thy greatest enemies,

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: Richard of Bordeaux, by me hither brought.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Exton, I thank thee not; for thou hast wrought

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: A deed of slander with thy fatal hand

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Upon my head and all this famous land.

lines.speaker: Sir Pierce of Exton
lines.text: From your own mouth, my lord, did I this deed.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: They love not poison that do poison need,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Nor do I thee: though I did wish him dead,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: I hate the murderer, love him murdered.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: The guilt of conscience take thou for thy labour,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: But neither my good word nor princely favour:

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: With Cain go wander thorough shade of night,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: And never show thy head by day nor light.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Lords, I protest my soul is full of woe,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: That blood should sprinkle me to make me grow:

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: Come, mourn with me for what I do lament,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: And put on sullen black incontinent.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: I'll make a voyage to the Holy Land,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: To wash this blood off from my guilty hand.

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: March sadly after; grace my mournings here,

lines.speaker: Henry Bolingbroke
lines.text: In weeping after this untimely bier.
